findings_not_failures.finding: When the entry write is refused, Run::restructure_and_entry and Run::submit_sequence_and_entry undo their committed structure / sequence step with undo(). undo() moves that step onto the redo history and replaces any redo history that existed before. A later redo therefore re-applies the structure or sequence change WITHOUT its entry, which is the split step both docs say cannot happen. It also discards the user's earlier redo steps. The refusal test checks only the undo history (run_restructure_and_entry.rs:69), so it cannot catch this. Reachable only when set_document_entry refuses after the structure edit was accepted (entry budget, cancellation).
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: save the redo stack before the edit and restore it after the rollback undo (as play_action does), then assert redo is nothing_to_redo after a refused entry write

findings_not_failures.finding: The new public, mutating, undoable Run::submit_sequence_and_entry is missing from the STU-AUT-147 command corpus RUN_COMMANDS. SMB-PS-ACTIONS-1's test corpus_lists_every_run_operation_with_recordability uses a fixed list, so it cannot see the gap. The method also writes no not_recordable entry under its own id: a recording names it document.submit_sequence. Its rollback undo() is not wrapped in quietly(), so a refused entry write adds a spurious history.undo not_recordable entry. restructure_and_entry, which SMB-PS-ACTIONS-1 rebased, does neither of these things.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: add a document.submit_sequence_and_entry entry to RUN_COMMANDS (recordable false); call note_unrecordable and run the inner submit and the rollback quietly, as restructure_and_entry does
findings_not_failures.evidence: comparison of the pub fns of impl Run in harness.rs with the RUN_COMMANDS method names at 2bc9103a: submit_sequence_and_entry is the only mutating Run operation that is absent

findings_not_failures.finding: Both W3C licences make permission conditional on 'the full text of this NOTICE in a location viewable to users of the redistributed or derivative work', plus the pre-existing notices and a notice of changes. The corrected NOTICE carries every element the brief asked for, each checked against the W3C pages on 2026-10-30: licence names and links, each document's notice with its years, dated version URIs and status, and a notice of changes. It points to the licence texts by URL ('The licence texts are at the URLs above') and does not include them. The brief allowed name plus link. Under the licences' own wording, a link is not enough wherever the shipped tables count as material derived from the documents.
